question: Assume today is 2026-10-24. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the total profits of China's industrial enterprises above designated size (规模以上工业企业利润总额) for January-September 2026 (the cumulative total, not the single month of September), in Chinese yuan (CNY; the release states it in 亿元, i.e. units of 100 million yuan), as it will be first reported in the National Bureau of Statistics of China's monthly release on profits of industrial enterprises.

target.what: Cumulative total profits of China's industrial enterprises above designated size (规模以上工业企业利润总额), January-September 2026, as first reported by the National Bureau of Statistics of China in units of 亿元 (100 million CNY). This is a year-to-date flow for 2026-01-01 through 2026-09-30, covering above-sca
target.publisher: National Bureau of Statistics of China (NBS)
target.caveats: The first reported figure is likely preliminary and subject to later revision. Coverage is the NBS above-designated-size industrial sample, which can change over time; profits are in current prices and not inflation-adjusted. The release may emphasize cumulative total and year-on-year growth. Altern

candidates.perspective: NBS monthly cumulative releases and historical seasonal pattern
candidates.hypothesis: The Jan-Sep 2026 cumulative profit total can be projected from the latest available Jan-Aug 2026 cumulative total plus an estimated September increment, guided by the historical share of September in Jan-Sep and by year-on-year growth patterns. The relationship is expected to be strong because the target is a cumulative flow with stable seasonal timing.
candidates.data_to_find: NBS cumulative industrial enterprise profit totals for Jan-Sep 2019-2025, Jan-Aug and Jan-Jul 2026, plus any pre-cutoff revisions. Also find monthly September increments and year-on-year growth rates for the same years. Minimum evidence: Jan-Aug 2026 cumulative total and at least three historical September shares of Jan-Sep.

a1.role: September 2026 single-month total profit growth factor relative to September 2025, dimensionless

methods.rationale: Starts from the observed January-August 2026 cumulative profit and adds a September 2026 increment equal to the September 2025 increment scaled by an assumed September 2026 year-on-year profit factor. This directly uses the latest cumulative level and the prior-year seasonal increment. The main uncertainty is the September 2026 growth factor; September 2025 was a high base and recent monthly growth slowed, so the factor is set below the prior-year pace but still positive. Shared dependency: p13 and p19 are the same NBS 2025 release and p3 is the 2026 NBS release.

p4.role: January-August 2026 cumulative operating revenue of China's above-scale industrial enterprises, in CNY

a2.role: January-September 2026 revenue divided by January-August 2026 revenue, dimensionless

a3.role: January-September 2026 operating revenue profit margin, fraction after code converts percent

methods.rationale: Uses the NBS identity profit equals revenue times profit margin. January-August 2026 revenue is observed; a2 extends it to January-September revenue using the 2025 seasonal revenue ratio; a3 sets the cumulative margin near the observed January-August 5.66% with a range. This route is independent of the reported January-August profit level and checks whether the profit increment is consistent with revenue and margin. Failure modes are a September revenue surprise or a margin shift.

p13.role: January-September 2025 cumulative total profit of China's above-scale industrial enterprises, in yuan, the prior-year reported level

a4.role: January-September 2026 cumulative total profit growth relative to the reported January-September 2025 level, raw fraction after code converts percent

methods.rationale: Applies an assumed raw cumulative growth rate to the reported January-September 2025 profit level. The growth assumption is anchored on the observed January-August 2026 level versus January-August 2025, adjusted for slower August single-month growth and positive September activity indicators. This route is simple but vulnerable to sample changes and to divergence between reported comparable-basis growth and raw level growth.

assumptions.name: September 2026 single-month industrial profit growth factor versus September 2025
assumptions.rationale: August 2026 single-month profit grew 4.2% y/y and July grew 11.2%; September 2026 industrial value added rose 5.5%, PPI rose 5.0%, export delivery value rose 17.0% and manufacturing PMI was 50.1. September 2025 was a high base with +21.6% single-month profit growth, so September 2026 growth is likely positive but below that. A factor of 1.07 means about +7%, with a wide range from -5% to +20%.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 single-month industrial profit growth is broadly in line with the August-September 2026 activity and price indicators and the high prior-year base.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 single-month industrial profit fell more than 5% or rose more than 20% year on year.

assumptions.name: January-September 2026 revenue divided by January-August 2026 revenue
assumptions.rationale: The 2025 NBS release shows January-September revenue of 102.08万亿元 against January-August revenue of 89.62万亿元, a ratio near 1.139. September 2026 PPI was +5.0%, value added +5.5% and export delivery value +17.0%, supporting a similar seasonal revenue increment. The range allows for weaker or stronger September sales.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 revenue seasonality is similar to 2025 and the above-scale sample remains broadly comparable.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 revenue was much weaker or stronger than the normal September increment, for example a September revenue collapse or a surge above 17% of the January-August total.

assumptions.name: January-September 2026 operating revenue profit margin
assumptions.rationale: The observed January-August 2026 margin is 5.66%, up 0.44 pp from a year earlier, and January-September 2025 was 5.26%. September 2026 producer prices rose but purchaser prices also rose, while capacity utilisation was modest. A margin near the January-August level is plausible, with the range covering moderate compression or expansion.
assumptions.applies_when: Aggregate industrial margin in September 2026 stays close to the January-August 2026 margin rather than being distorted by a few sectors.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 aggregate industrial margin fell below 5.4% or rose above 6.0%.

assumptions.name: January-September 2026 cumulative industrial profit growth relative to the reported January-September 2025 level
assumptions.rationale: The reported January-August 2026 level of 52719.8亿元 against the January-August 2025 level of 46929.7亿元 implies low-teens raw growth, while the NBS comparable-basis growth was 15.7%. August 2026 single-month growth slowed to 4.2%, but September activity and price indicators were positive. A raw cumulative growth rate around 11.5% is used, with a wide range for sample and base effects.
assumptions.applies_when: The January-September 2026 reported level grows from the January-September 2025 reported level at a raw rate consistent with recent monthly growth and sample continuity.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that January-September 2026 cumulative profit growth relative to the prior-year reported level was below 8% or above 15%.

p5.role: January-August 2026 operating revenue profit margin, fraction after code converts percent

methods.rationale: NBS accounting identity: cumulative profit = cumulative revenue × profit margin. Jan-Sep 2026 revenue is approximated by observed Jan-Aug 2026 revenue p42 times the Jan-Sep 2025 / Jan-Aug 2025 revenue ratio, where Jan-Aug 2025 revenue is inferred as p19/p20. That revenue is multiplied by the observed Jan-Aug 2026 margin p5 and a small margin-change factor a3. It uses a different observed base from m2 but shares p19 and the margin evidence; p20 is a rounded margin, adding minor noise to inferred Jan-Aug 2025 revenue. Failure modes: September 2026 revenue seasonality differs from 2025, the margin change a3 is wrong, or p20 rounding materially distorts the 2025 revenue ratio.

It is informed by the Jan-Aug 2026 raw level versus Jan-Aug 2025, the high September 2025 base, and recent single-month deceleration. It shares p13 with m1 and m2 and shares macro drivers with a1, so it is not fully independent. Failure modes: a sample/comparable-basis shift, a revision to p13, or an a4 error from the high September 2025 base or cost squeeze.

assumptions.name: September 2026 single-month industrial profit growth factor versus September 2025
assumptions.rationale: August 2026 single-month profit growth was +4.2% after +11.2% in July, while September 2025 had a high +21.6% base. September 2026 activity was firm: industrial value added +5.5%, PPI +5.0%, export delivery +17.0%, but purchase prices +6.9% and the PMI input-output price gap suggest margin pressure. I center on modest positive single-month growth and allow a wide downside for the high base and cost squeeze.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 above-scale industrial profit growth is broadly in line with recent single-month momentum and September activity/price indicators; no major sample change or policy shock.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 single-month profit fell sharply or surged outside the assumed range, a major NBS sample/comparable-basis revision, or a large policy shock to costs or demand.

assumptions.name: January-September 2026 operating revenue profit margin relative to the January-August 2026 margin
assumptions.rationale: Jan-Aug 2026 margin was 5.66%; August single-month margin was 5.7% versus July 5.4%. September PPI reflation helps revenue, but purchase prices rose faster and the PMI input-output price gap points to cost pressure. The cumulative Jan-Sep margin should stay close to the Jan-Aug margin, with a small allowance for September margin composition.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 margin remains close to recent monthly and cumulative margins; no abrupt cost or price shock.
assumptions.falsified_by: September margin evidence outside the range, e.g. a sharp collapse in margins due to input costs or a large policy-driven price change.

assumptions.name: January-September 2026 raw cumulative industrial profit growth relative to the reported January-September 2025 level
assumptions.rationale: Jan-Aug 2026 comparable-basis profit growth was +15.7%, but raw level growth versus Jan-Aug 2025 is lower because NBS growth is comparable-basis and the sample can change. September 2025 had a high +21.6% single-month base, and recent single-month growth slowed to +4.2% in August. I therefore use a raw cumulative growth rate in the low teens, not the comparable-basis 15.7%, with a wide range reflecting forecast dispersion and cost-squeeze risk.
assumptions.applies_when: The reported Jan-Sep 2025 level p13 is the appropriate base after allowing for sample/comparable-basis differences; September 2026 profit growth is near recent momentum.
assumptions.falsified_by: A large NBS sample/comparable-basis change, a revision to p13, or evidence that September 2026 profit growth is far from the assumed range.

previous_assumptions.name: September 2026 single-month industrial profit growth factor versus September 2025
previous_assumptions.rationale: August 2026 single-month profit growth was +4.2% (p2/p29/p48) after +11.2% in July (p30/p383), while September 2025 had a high +21.6% base (p10). September 2026 activity was firm—IP +5.5% (p65/p90), PPI +5.0% (p68/p391), export delivery +17.0% (p95)—but purchase prices +6.9% (p71/p393) and the PMI input-output price gap (p241/p242) suggest margin pressure. I center near modest positive growth and allow a wide downside.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 above-scale industrial profit growth is broadly in line with recent single-month momentum and September activity/price indicators; no major sample change or policy shock.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 profit fell sharply or surged, e.g., monthly profit growth outside the range, a major NBS sample revision, or a large policy shock to costs or demand.

previous_assumptions.name: January-September 2026 revenue divided by January-August 2026 revenue
previous_assumptions.rationale: In 2025 the Jan-Sep/Jan-Aug revenue ratio was about 1.139, using p11 and the Jan-Aug 2025 revenue implied by p19 and p20. September 2026 nominal revenue should grow with IP +5.5% and PPI +5.0%, but August 2026 single-month revenue growth was only +5.3% (p34/p353), so I keep the ratio near the 2025 seasonal value with a modest range.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 revenue seasonality and nominal growth are similar to the 2025 pattern and recent monthly revenue growth.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: September 2026 revenue growth far outside the implied range, e.g., a sharp export collapse or a price spike not captured by the PPI and IP indicators.

previous_assumptions.name: January-September 2026 operating revenue profit margin
previous_assumptions.rationale: Jan-Aug 2026 margin was 5.66% (p5/p40/p327); August single-month margin was 5.7% (p217) versus July 5.4% (p218). September PPI reflation helps revenue, but purchase prices rose faster (p71/p393) and the PMI input-output price gap (p241/p242) points to cost pressure, so the cumulative margin should stay near the Jan-Aug level.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 margin remains close to the recent monthly and cumulative margins; no abrupt cost or price shock.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: September margin evidence outside the range, e.g., a sharp collapse in margins due to input costs or a large policy-driven price change.

previous_assumptions.name: January-September 2026 raw cumulative industrial profit growth relative to the reported January-September 2025 level
previous_assumptions.rationale: Jan-Aug 2026 comparable-basis profit growth was +15.7% (p1), but raw level growth versus p19 is lower because NBS growth is comparable-basis and the sample can change. September 2025 had a high +21.6% single-month base (p10), and recent single-month growth slowed to +4.2% in August (p2/p29). I therefore use a raw cumulative growth rate in the low teens, not the comparable-basis 15.7%, with a wide range reflecting forecast dispersion (p362-p376) and cost-squeeze risk.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: The reported Jan-Sep 2025 level p13 is the appropriate base after allowing for sample/comparable-basis differences; September 2026 profit growth is near recent momentum.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: A large NBS sample/comparable-basis change, a revision to p13, or evidence that September 2026 profit growth is far from the assumed range.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
